Identity.History: Pagondas was a prominent Theban general and statesman of the late 5th century BC, best known for commanding the Boeotian army at the Battle of Delium in 424 BC during the Peloponnesian War. Facing an Athenian invasion of Boeotia, Pagondas persuaded the Boeotians to give battle and arranged the Theban contingent in an unusually deep formation—about twenty-five ranks—while also using cavalry decisively against the exposed Athenian flank. The resulting Boeotian victory made Delium one of Athens’ most serious land defeats of the war. Pagondas’ battlefield innovations, especially his emphasis on depth and concentrated force, are often seen as important precedents for the later tactics of Epaminondas and the great Theban armies of the 4th century BC.
